title: IELTS scoring in detail
author: IELTS Partners
access: Official web guidance reviewed, 9 September 2026
supports: Four separate skill scores, overall aggregation, band definitions and form-dependent raw-score conversion.
does_not_support: A completion certificate, vocabulary count, fixed study duration or an app-generated score guaranteeing an official band.

title: IELTS Academic: Listening test format
author: IELTS Partners
access: Official web guidance reviewed
supports: Four parts, 40 questions, once-only examination audio and the listening task families.
does_not_support: Treating single-word TTS, memorised transcripts or teacher-supported listening as examination-equivalent evidence.

title: IELTS Academic: Reading test format
author: IELTS Partners
access: Official web guidance reviewed
supports: Three sections, 40 questions, 60 minutes, passage characteristics and reading task families.
does_not_support: One keyword-matching strategy or a universal question-order rule for every task family.

title: IELTS Academic: Writing test format
author: IELTS Partners
access: Official web guidance reviewed
supports: Two writing tasks, minimum word counts, total timing and the greater weighting of Task 2.
does_not_support: A mandatory five-paragraph template or a requirement to use rare words.

title: IELTS Academic: Speaking test format
author: IELTS Partners
access: Official web guidance reviewed
supports: The three-part interview and its timing and interaction demands.
does_not_support: Assessing conversational ability solely through shadowing or reading a prepared answer.

title: IELTS Writing Band Descriptors, updated May 2023
author: IELTS Partners
access: Official PDF text and high-band descriptor tables inspected
supports: Analytic criteria for Task 1 and Task 2, including accurate task fulfilment, coherence, lexical precision and grammatical control.
does_not_support: Labelling the original examples in this package examiner-certified Band 9 answers.

title: IELTS Speaking Band Descriptors
author: IELTS Partners
access: Official PDF text and descriptor table inspected
supports: Fluency/coherence, lexical resource, grammatical range/accuracy and pronunciation criteria.
does_not_support: A native-accent requirement or an automatic pronunciation-to-band conversion.

title: IELTS and the CEFR
author: IELTS Partners
access: Official web guidance reviewed
supports: Caution when comparing different proficiency scales.
does_not_support: A one-to-one IELTS/CEFR conversion or a CEFR-labelled lesson conferring an IELTS score.

title: IELTS Academic sample test questions
author: IELTS Partners
access: Official sample-task index and format descriptions reviewed; protected tests not reproduced
supports: Examples of authentic task presentation and answer constraints.
does_not_support: Redistributing the complete commercial Cambridge test bank inside Vocora.

title: Updates to IELTS test delivery
author: IELTS Partners
access: Official announcement of 5 March 2026 reviewed
supports: The announced mid-2026 move towards computer delivery, with market-dependent implementation and selected Writing on Paper options.
does_not_support: Assuming identical availability or transition dates in every country.

title: IELTS on computer
author: IDP IELTS Germany
access: Official delivery guidance reviewed
supports: Computer-listening answer entry and two minutes of final answer checking.
does_not_support: Adding the legacy ten-minute paper transfer allowance to a computer mock.

title: Test-Enhanced Learning: Taking Memory Tests Improves Long-Term Retention
author: Roediger, H. L., III, & Karpicke, J. D.
access: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record reviewed
supports: Retrieval can improve delayed retention relative to repeated study.
does_not_support: The exact Vocora lesson order, a universal mastery percentage or IELTS 3-to-9 effectiveness.

title: The Effects of Spaced Practice on Second Language Learning: A Meta-Analysis
author: Kim, S. K., & Webb, S.
access: Publisher abstract and study summary reviewed
supports: Spacing benefits L2 learning; timing and retention interval matter.
does_not_support: One optimal 1-3-7-14-day schedule for every learner, word and skill.

title: The Effects of Receptive and Productive Learning of Word Pairs on Vocabulary Knowledge
author: Webb, S.
access: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record reviewed
supports: Different learning operations develop different dimensions of word knowledge.
does_not_support: Multiple-choice recognition being equivalent to productive mastery.

title: The Effects of Vocabulary Learning on Collocation and Meaning
author: Webb, S., & Kagimoto, E.
access: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record reviewed
supports: Focused vocabulary work can develop collocation and meaning knowledge.
does_not_support: Teaching every possible collocation together or mechanically replacing every word with a synonym.

title: The four strands
author: Nation, I. S. P.
access: Publisher bibliographic record and author/university summaries reviewed
supports: Balancing meaning-focused input, meaning-focused output, language-focused learning and fluency development.
does_not_support: A clinical-trial proof that exactly 25% per strand is optimal for this app.

title: Oral Feedback in Classroom SLA: A Meta-Analysis
author: Lyster, R., & Saito, K.
access: Publisher abstract reviewed
supports: Corrective feedback can support classroom L2 development, including prompted learner repair.
does_not_support: Assuming a speech model provides feedback of the same validity as the studied classroom interventions.

title: The Efficacy of Written Corrective Feedback in Improving L2 Written Accuracy: A Meta-Analysis
author: Kang, E., & Han, Z.
access: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record reviewed
supports: Written corrective feedback can improve grammatical accuracy, with contextual moderators.
does_not_support: Grammar correction alone producing a high IELTS Task Response or Coherence score.

title: Exploring the possibilities of integrating communicative AI into the IELTS test preparation process
author: Perrotta, C., Knoch, U., Selwyn, N., & Mohammadi, S.
access: Report introduction, methods and assessment limitations reviewed
supports: AI preparation has potential, but contextual awareness, bias, reliability and consistency remain concerns.
does_not_support: Uncalibrated AI scores certifying IELTS 9 or an app-only 3-to-9 guarantee.

title: Investigating test preparation practices: Reducing risks
author: Chappell, P., Yates, L., & Benson, P.
access: Research report summary, methods and conclusions reviewed
supports: Learner experiences motivate clear assessment criteria and support for using preparation strategies.
does_not_support: Anecdotes or reported practices establishing the causal effectiveness of this curriculum.

title: Investigation of relationships between learner background, linguistic progression and score gain on IELTS
author: Kang, O., Ahn, H., Yaw, K., & Chung, S.-Y.
access: Official report summary reviewed; authors not independently transcribed
supports: Progress differs among learners and depends on starting level and study conditions.
does_not_support: Linear extrapolation from a short preparation period to a guaranteed six-band gain.

author: Norris, J. M., & Ortega, L.
access: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record reviewed
supports: Focused instruction supports target-oriented L2 gains; explicit attention to form can be useful.
does_not_support: A grammar-only curriculum or rule-quiz success demonstrating spontaneous communicative proficiency.

title: A Meta-Analysis of Extensive Reading Research
author: Nakanishi, T.
access: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record reviewed
supports: Extensive reading is supported as a component of reading development.
does_not_support: A fixed daily minute count, a particular generated library or a guaranteed IELTS reading band.

title: Fluency Training in the ESL Classroom: An Experimental Study of Fluency Development and Proceduralization
author: de Jong, N., & Perfetti, C. A.
access: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record reviewed
supports: Speech repetition can contribute to fluency development; later transfer still needs assessment.
does_not_support: Making every answer shorter, forcing speed at the expense of intelligibility, or memorisation counting as fresh exam performance.

supports: Guided planning, monitoring and evaluation supported listening development in the studied setting.
does_not_support: The exact Vocora AI workflow being validated, or giving replay and prediction hints during a scored IELTS simulation.
